# Resource: stripe_account_external_account

A bank account that a connected account is paid out to. `terraform destroy` deletes it. The first bank account added in a currency is its default: bank accounts created in one apply are added in no fixed order, so order them with `depends_on` or set `default_for_currency`. Stripe refuses `default_for_currency = false` on an account's first bank account in a currency. The bank account is also served as `bank_accounts` in Stripe's API: it is the same object. Stripe never returns the `account_number`, so state keeps the value you configured and treats it as sensitive. Only `account_holder_name`, `account_holder_type`, `default_for_currency` and `metadata` change in place; changing anything else creates a new bank account.

~> Stripe refuses to delete the default bank account of a currency; make another bank account the default first, or remove this one from the state before destroying the account, which deletes its bank accounts. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace it, fail at plan time for such an account external account. To stop managing one, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_account" "seller" {
  type    = "custom"
  country = "US"

  # A custom account must request at least one capability.
  capabilities = {
    transfers = { requested = true }
  }
}

# Stripe's test bank account for the United States. In live mode, pass the seller's own
# routing and account numbers from a sensitive variable.
resource "stripe_account_external_account" "payouts" {
  account        = stripe_account.seller.id
  country        = "US"
  currency       = "usd"
  routing_number = "110000000"
  account_number = "000123456789"

  account_holder_name = "Acme Supplies"
  account_holder_type = "company"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `account` - (Required) The ID of the parent object. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `account_number` - (Required, Sensitive) Changing it replaces the resource.
* `country` - (Required) Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO code for the currency](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts) paid out to the bank account. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `routing_number` - (Required) The routing transit number for the bank account. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `account_holder_name` - (Optional) The name of the person or business that owns the bank account. Default: not sent.
* `account_holder_type` - (Optional) The type of entity that holds the account. This can be either `individual` or `company`. Possible values: `company`, `individual`. Default: not sent.
* `default_for_currency` - (Optional) When set to true, or if this is the first external account added in this currency, this account becomes the default external account for its currency. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `account_type` - The bank account type. This can only be `checking` or `savings` in most countries. In Japan, this can only be `futsu` or `toza`.
* `available_payout_methods` - A set of available payout methods for this bank account. Only values from this set should be passed as the `method` when creating a payout.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the routing number (e.g., `WELLS FARGO`).
* `customer` - The ID of the customer that the bank account is associated with.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `future_requirements` - Information about the [upcoming new requirements for the bank account](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/custom-accounts/future-requirements), including what information needs to be collected, and by when. See [`future_requirements`](#future_requirements) below.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the bank account number.
* `requirements` - Information about the requirements for the bank account, including what information needs to be collected. See [`requirements`](#requirements) below.
* `status` - For bank accounts, possible values are `new`, `validated`, `verified`, `verification_failed`, `tokenized_account_number_deactivated` or `errored`. A bank account that hasn't had any activity or validation performed is `new`. If Stripe can determine that the bank account exists, its status will be `validated`. Note that there often isn’t enough information to know (e.g., for smaller credit unions), and the validation is not always run. If customer bank account verification has succeeded, the bank account status will be `verified`. If the verification failed for any reason, such as microdeposit failure, the status will be `verification_failed`. If the status is `tokenized_account_number_deactivated`, the account utilizes a tokenized account number which has been deactivated due to expiration or revocation. This account will need to be reverified to continue using it for money movement. If a payout sent to this bank account fails, we'll set the status to `errored` and will not continue to send [scheduled payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#payout-schedule) until the bank details are updated. For external accounts, possible values are `new`, `errored`, `verification_failed`, and `tokenized_account_number_deactivated`. If a payout fails, the status is set to `errored` and scheduled payouts are stopped until account details are updated. In the US and India, if we can't [verify the owner of the bank account](https://support.stripe.com/questions/bank-account-ownership-verification), we'll set the status to `verification_failed`. Other validations aren't run against external accounts because they're only used for payouts. This means the other statuses don't apply.

<a id="future_requirements"></a>
### `future_requirements`

The `future_requirements` attribute supports:

* `currently_due` - Fields that need to be resolved to keep the external account enabled. If not resolved by `current_deadline`, these fields will appear in `past_due` as well, and the account is disabled.
* `errors` - Fields that are `currently_due` and need to be collected again because validation or verification failed. See [`future_requirements.errors`](#future_requirements.errors) below.
* `past_due` - Fields that haven't been resolved by `current_deadline`. These fields need to be resolved to enable the external account.
* `pending_verification` - Fields that are being reviewed, or might become required depending on the results of a review. If the review fails, these fields can move to `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives`. Fields might appear in `eventually_due`, `currently_due`, `past_due` or `alternatives` and in `pending_verification` if one verification fails but another is still pending.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing an account external account whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_account_external_account.payouts

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_account_external_account.payouts
```

The account external account stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

The ID is the account ID and the bank account ID, separated by a slash.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import an account external account using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_account_external_account.payouts
  id = "acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK/ba_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_account_external_account.payouts
  identity = {
    account = "acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK"
    id      = "ba_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `account` (String) The ID of the parent account.
* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the account external account.

Using `terraform import`, import an account external account using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_account_external_account.payouts acct_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK/ba_1Nv0FGQ9RKHgCVdK
```

~> Stripe never returns the account number, so an imported bank account has none in state: a configuration that sets `account_number` plans a replacement unless it ignores changes to it with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [account_number] }`.
